about.title: Norco Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Norco's mix of horse-property roads, the I-15 corridor, and busy stretches like Hamner Avenue and River Road means collisions here happen in a range of settings, from highway rear-enders to intersection crashes near 6th Street. Riverside County crash data shows a steady flow of injury collisions each year, with Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. showing up often in reported crash timing. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the period right after matters: California law gives you a limited window to act, insurance adjusters may ask for a recorded statement early, and evidence like skid marks or vehicle damage can fade fast. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free service that connects injured Norco residents with an independent personal injury attorney who works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. We can help you take that first step without guessing at what to do next.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury claim, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity (like a road authority) may be responsible. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it passes.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for the crash, you can still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. Insurers know this and often push blame onto you early to lower what they pay.

items.title: What You Say Can Be Used to Limit Your Claim
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a California car accident case, but a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to undercut your claim before you've even seen a doctor. It's worth having someone in your corner before that call happens.

items.question: I was in a crash near the I-15 and Hamner Avenue interchange. Does it matter where in Norco this happened?
items.answer: The location can affect who's involved, for example, whether a government road authority might share responsibility, which can shorten your filing deadline to as little as six months. An independent attorney can look at the specifics of where and how it happened and explain what deadlines apply to your case.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company already called me. Should I give them a recorded statement?
items.answer: You're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's generally wise to speak with an attorney first. Statements made early, before you know the full extent of your injuries, can sometimes be used to reduce what you're offered later.

items.question: How much will it cost me to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost or obligation to move forward.
